q: Brasília, considered the biggest planning exercise of the 20th century, was completed within four years using how many workers?
ref: History of city planning: Lucio Costa
n: 600,000 workers finished Brasília within 4 years.

q: Which architect was commissioned by Pope Sixtus V to prepare a street plan for Rome, marking key points in the city with tall obelisks as visual accents?
ref: History of city planning: Rome 1500s
n: Domenico Fontana was commissioned by Pope Sixtus V to prepare and establish a street plan/framework for the growth of Rome, marking key points with tall obelisks.

q: English social reformer Robert Owen constructed an industrial village at New Lanark based on the concept of:
ref: History of city planning
n: Owen constructed and operated an industrial village at New Lanark, a social and manufacturing community conceptualized as the "Village of Unity and Mutual Cooperation."

q: Wright and Stein's regional approach proposed constellations of smaller communities, as at which New Jersey town?
ref: History of city planning: Henry Wright and Clarence Stein
n: The core of constellations of smaller communities is exemplified by Radburn, New Jersey.

q: British-born architect Ralph Erskine built the remarkable Byker Wall, a redevelopment housing project designed for:
o: Maximum density regardless of resident input
ref: History of city planning: Ralph Erskine
n: The Byker Wall was designed for continuous dialogue with the residents.

q: The People's Homesite and Housing Corporation (PHHC) was established primarily to address:
o: Rising housing demand, especially in the cities
Zoning of new industrial estates near ports
Land reform for tenant farmers in the provinces
ref: History of city planning: Philippine Republic
n: PHHC was established to address growing housing needs, especially in urban centers, and was notably involved in developing Quezon City and large housing subdivisions.

q: Haussmann's rebuilding made Paris the "City of Lights" and a model for which American movement led by Daniel Burnham?
ref: History of city planning: Paris 1800s
n: Paris became the model for the American City Beautiful Era, adopted by Daniel Burnham.

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: George Cadbury relocated his chocolate factory to Bournville outside Birmingham (1879–1895), notable for being open to workers:
ref: History of city planning: New Communities
n: Bournville was open to workers regardless of race or religion.

q: In "The New Exploration: A Philosophy of Regional Planning," Benton Mackaye coined the interdependent concepts of the "townless highway" and the:
ref: History of city planning: Benton Mackaye
n: Mackaye spoke of the "townless highway" and "highwayless town" as mutually interdependent.

q: Patrick Geddes coined the term "conurbation" to describe:
o: A satellite town set apart by a greenbelt
Towns that have grown together into one mass
A garden suburb on the edge of a city
A linear settlement strung along a road
ref: History of city planning: Patrick Geddes
n: Geddes coined "conurbation," meaning a conglomeration of town aggregates.

q: Thomas Adams directed the 8-volume 1928 survey for the New York City Metropolitan Area (RPAA/RPA), which was criticized for its limits on:
ref: History of city planning: Thomas Adams
n: The 8-volume survey directed by Adams was criticized for its limits on physical scope.

q: Norbert Wiener's ideas were instrumental in changing the planning paradigm from production of blueprints towards planning as:
o: A continuous series of controls over development
A purely aesthetic exercise in civic design
A single master plan drawn once and fixed
A purely legal exercise in drafting zoning codes
ref: History of city planning: Norbert Wiener
n: Wiener helped shift planning from static blueprints to continuous controls over development, aided by devices that model or simulate the development process.

q: Jane Jacobs argued that there was nothing wrong with high urban densities of people as long as they did not entail:
ref: History of city planning: Jane Jacobs
n: Jacobs argued high densities were fine if they did not entail overcrowding in buildings, and prescribed mixed functions/land uses and mixed-age blocks to serve different purposes and schedules.

q: The Convent (Convento) in a Spanish colonial town was:
o: The residence of the priests or friars, by the church
The seat of the governor and the town's officials
The town market for trade and tax collection
The parish school run by the religious orders
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period — Key Elements
n: The Convento was the residence of priests or friars, typically attached to or near the church.

q: In what year did Patrick Geddes write "Cities in Evolution"?
ref: History of city planning: Patrick Geddes
n: Geddes wrote Cities in Evolution in 1915 (earlier works were City Development in 1904 and Civics as Applied Sociology in 1905).

q: American Edgar Chambless proposed a city with all vehicles running on:
o: The roof of one continuous building
ref: History of city planning
n: Chambless proposed a city with all vehicles running on the rooftops of a continuous building.

q: Rome in the 1500s was confronted with problems of circulation, defense, water supply, and:
ref: History of city planning: Rome 1500s
n: Rome faced problems of circulation, defense, water supply, and sanitation, prompting Popes to undertake civic improvement projects.

s: Modern Architecture and Planning — Eliel Saarinen
q: In 1943, Eliel Saarinen wrote "The City," proposing:
ref: History of city planning: Eliel Saarinen
n: "The City" (1943) proposed the decentralization of large cities.

q: During the American Era, there were no local planning institutions, and Filipino planners were trained:
o: At the UP Institute of Planning
ref: History of city planning: American Era
n: There were no local planning institutions in this era; Filipino planners were trained abroad.

q: Viennese architect Christopher Alexander developed the idea that for things to become alive and beautiful, it is necessary for people to be:
o: Directly involved in the act of construction
ref: History of city planning: Christopher Alexander
n: Alexander believed people must be directly involved in the act of construction, rather than fiddling, for things to become alive and beautiful.

q: According to Geddes, the stages in the creation of conurbations follow the sequence:
ref: History of city planning: Patrick Geddes
n: The stages are Inflow, Build up, Backflow (center slums), then Sprawling mass (central blight).

q: Which of these is NOT a Marcos-era Philippine planning project?
ref: History of city planning: Marcos Regime
n: Radburn, New Jersey is a U.S. New Communities Movement project, not one of the Marcos-era Philippine projects (Metro Manila Strategic Plan, Tondo Foreshore Project, BLISS housing).

q: The Spanish "reduccion system" was a policy of gathering scattered indigenous populations into centralized villages or towns primarily to facilitate administration, tax collection, evangelization, and:
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period — Urban Impact
n: The reduccion system facilitated administration, tax collection, evangelization, and social control.

q: Constantine Doxiadis published his "Ekistic Grids," a system for:
o: Zoning industrial districts away from housing
Mapping the stages of conurbation growth
Recording planning data and ordering the process
Laying out garden cities on a regular grid
ref: History of city planning: Constantine Doxiadis
n: The Ekistic Grids were a system for recording planning data and ordering the planning process.

q: Spanish colonial towns in the Philippines, the "pueblos", were built around which system?
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period
n: Pueblos were structured around the reduccion system.

q: Which two works are associated with Daniel Burnham, "Father of American City Planning"?
o: Cities in Evolution and Garden Cities of To-morrow
Plan of Chicago (1909) and Planning the Region of Chicago
Broadacre City and The Disappearing City
The City in History and The Culture of Cities
ref: History of city planning: Daniel Burnham
n: Burnham wrote the Plan for Chicago (1909) and Planning the Region of Chicago (1956), his greatest achievement being the Chicago Plan of 1909.

q: Working under a commission chaired by Stein, Henry Wright produced a report explaining how New York transformed from a city of small trade centers into a financial and managerial center, titled:
o: Regional Plan of New York and Its Environs
Survey of the Regional Planning Association of America
Report of the Commission of Housing and Regional Planning (New York)
ref: History of city planning: Henry Wright and Clarence Stein
n: Wright, working under Stein's commission, produced this report on New York's development.

s: Conservationist & Park Movement — Frederick Law Olmstead
q: Which New York park did Frederick Law Olmsted, "Father of Landscape Architecture", design?
ref: History of city planning: Conservationist & Park Movement
n: Olmstead is associated with the American park system and designed Central Park, New York, among other projects.

q: The Metro Manila Commission (MMC), established in 1975 under PD 824 to centralize governance of Metro Manila, was chaired during its early years by:
ref: History of city planning: Marcos Regime
n: The MMC was chaired by Imelda Marcos during its early years.

q: Medieval towns typically grew around which protective centers?
o: A fortress or a river crossing only
A university or a cathedral only
ref: History of city planning: Medieval Times
n: Growth of towns around either a monastery or a castle relied on protective town walls or fortification for security.

q: Leslie Patrick Abercrombie (1879–1957), British, pioneered regional planning for the Doncaster area (1920–1922) and East Kent, and was involved in the:
ref: History of city planning: Leslie Patrick Abercrombie
n: Abercrombie was involved in the Greater London Plan, using open space as a structuring element.

q: Scottish architect James Craig laid out linear new towns with plazas, grid houses and open spaces on a plateau overlooking which city?
ref: History of city planning
n: James Craig planned linear new towns for Edinburgh, with interconnected plazas, grid houses, and open spaces on a plateau overlooking the city.

q: In the 1930s, Frank Lloyd Wright wrote "The Disappearing City" and later "Broadacres," proposing that every family live on:
ref: History of city planning: Frank Lloyd Wright
n: Wright proposed every family live on an acre of land, with the city built by its inhabitants using mass-produced components.

q: Albert Speer (1905–1981) was tasked by Hitler with planning the reconstruction of:
ref: History of city planning: The City Beautiful Era
n: Albert Speer was tasked by Hitler to plan the reconstruction of Berlin.

q: The 1909 Chicago Plan was heavily criticized as "centro-centrist," planned as an aristocratic city for merchant princes, with scant attention to:
ref: History of city planning: Daniel Burnham
n: Mumford castigated the plan as cosmetic, comparing it to totalitarian planning; health and sanitation were almost nowhere addressed and it devoted scant attention to zoning.

q: The Market (Tiangge or Pamilihan) in the plaza complex was located near the plaza for accessibility and served as a space for trade, taxation, and:
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period — Key Elements
n: The market was a space for trade, taxation, and economic control.

q: Richard Sennett cited the 1972 demolition of which housing project, blown up 17 years after completion, as a symbol of what went wrong with urban renewal?
ref: History of city planning: Richard Sennett
n: The Pruitt-Igoe Housing Project, 33 identical blocks with 2,800 apartments (completed 1955–56, designed by Minoru Yamasaki), was demolished in 1972 and became a symbol of what was wrong with urban renewal.

q: Rectilinear/gridded land plotting associated with the plow in the Ancient World was used in all of the following EXCEPT:
ref: History of city planning: Ancient World
n: Grid plotting was used in ancient Greek towns, Roman colonial outposts, and Indian, Chinese, and pre-Columbian cities — not medieval fortress towns, which belong to a later period.

q: Leon Battista Alberti is remembered as the foremost early theoretician for his concept of:
o: Garden cities ringed by open greenbelts
Broadacre cities of one family per acre
Linear cities strung along a utility spine
ref: History of city planning: Renaissance
n: Alberti is remembered for his "ideal cities" — star-shaped plans with streets radiating from a central point.

q: John Gwynn's 1766 plan "London and Westminster Improved" heralded what era of building in London?
ref: History of city planning
n: The plan heralded a Golden Age of building London.

q: The Home Financing Corporation (HFC) provided long-term financing for housing, including:
ref: History of city planning: Philippine Republic
n: HFC provided long-term financing for housing, including home mortgages and loans.

q: Italian futurist Antonio Sant'Elia's "La Città Nuova" provided a vision of an enormous metropolis based on:
o: Religious hierarchy around a central cathedral
Motion: vertical and horizontal circulation everywhere
ref: History of city planning: Antonio Sant'Elia
n: Sant'Elia's vision was based on motion, with every element of its design implying vertical and horizontal circulation.

s: Modern Architecture and Planning — Eliel Saarinen
q: Eliel Saarinen's prize-winning plan for Helsinki featured an overall circulation pattern whose elements suited the:
ref: History of city planning: Eliel Saarinen
n: Saarinen's Helsinki plan featured orderly, distinct community open space with a circulation pattern suited to the island and bay topography.

q: Constantine Doxiadis approached town planning as a science incorporating contributions from sociologists, geographers, economists, and other disciplines, calling this total rational and human approach:
ref: History of city planning: Constantine Doxiadis
n: Doxiadis called his approach "Ekistics" — the science of human settlements.

q: Le Corbusier's "La Ville Radieuse" (Radiant City, 1935) aimed to decongest city centers by doing what?
o: Spreading people evenly at low density
Moving all industry out to the country
Banning cars from the central district
Building high on a small part of the ground
ref: History of city planning: Le Corbusier
n: La Ville Radieuse aimed to decongest centers by increasing density through high building on a small part of the total ground area.

q: Houses of the Principalia (local elite) were typically located closest to the plaza, because their proximity symbolized:
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period — Key Elements
n: Principalia houses were located closest to the plaza, symbolizing power and prestige.

q: Architect-theorist Claude Nicolas Ledoux's principal work, Chaux, was a town designed for:
ref: History of city planning: Early 19th Century
n: Ledoux's principal work was Chaux, a town for salt workers in France, advocating informal grouping of houses and an ideal plan for workers' self-sufficiency.

s: Conservationist & Park Movement — Frederick Law Olmstead
q: Olmstead's 1880 plan connecting a system of parks in Boston is known as:
ref: History of city planning: Conservationist & Park Movement
n: Olmstead created The Emerald Necklace Plan for Boston in 1880.

q: In Roman town planning, the "perfected enclosed urban and architectural space" typically featured colonnaded plazas ending with:
ref: History of city planning: Ancient Rome
n: Perfected enclosed urban and architectural space refers to colonnaded plazas with a temple or basilica at the end of the space.

q: According to Kenzo Tange, once a city passes 2 or 3 million people, communication becomes inefficient in which city form?
o: A garden-city form ringed by greenbelts
A gridiron form with a regular street net
A radiocentric form grown without a plan
A linear form strung along a main axis
ref: History of city planning: Kenzo Tange
n: Tange held that beyond 2–3 million, communication becomes inefficient in a radiocentric city form created by spontaneous growth.

q: "CCPC", one of the planning bodies created in the Commonwealth period, stands for what?
ref: History of city planning: Commonwealth Period
n: CCPC stands for the Capital City Planning Commission.

q: Which planning-education institutions were created during the Marcos regime?
o: HLURB and the Metro Manila Development Authority
NHA and the National Economic Development Authority
NUPC and the Capital City Planning Commission
UP Institute of Planning and the PIEP
ref: History of city planning: Marcos Regime
n: The Marcos Regime saw the creation of the UP Institute of Planning and the Philippine Institute of Environmental Planners.

s: Town & Country Planning Act of 1947 in Britain
q: The Town and Country Planning Act of 1958 in Britain was essentially spatial, concerned with the spatial impact of many kinds of problems and:
ref: History of city planning: Town & Country Planning Act
n: It was concerned with spatial impact of problems and the spatial coordination of many different policies.

q: Pierre Charles L'Enfant, a French American engineer, is known for preparing the plan for:
ref: History of city planning: Renaissance era entries
n: L'Enfant prepared the plan for Washington, D.C.

q: During the Marcos Regime, in terms of economic development, the Philippines ranked as:
ref: History of city planning: Marcos Regime
n: In terms of economic development, the Philippines was no. 2 in Southeast Asia during this period.

q: French architect Tony Garnier designed a hypothetical industrial town with a definite center and a linear structure emphasizing zoning and separation of urban functions, called:
ref: History of city planning
n: Garnier designed "Une Cité Industrielle," anticipating modern zoning through separation of city parts and urban functions.

q: Regional planning is said to have started with Patrick Geddes (1854–1932), whose ideas derived from Scottish culture are summed up in the famous dictum:
o: "The city is a machine for living"
ref: History of city planning: Patrick Geddes
n: "Survey before Plan" comes from Geddes.

s: Ancient Greece (500–400 B.C.) — Hippodamus of Miletus
q: Which Greek architect planned Priene and Piraeus on a geometric grid of streets?
ref: History of city planning: Ancient Greece
n: Hippodamus of Miletus, called the Father of Town Planning, planned Priene and Piraeus with geometric designs and gridiron streets.

q: The City Beautiful movement's most spectacular manifestations occurred between 1910 and 1935, eventually giving way to city functional concepts that included:
ref: History of city planning: The City Beautiful Era
n: The movement gave way to city functional concepts that included zoning.

q: Medieval town street patterns generally featured:
o: Radial streets with a central piazza
ref: History of city planning: Medieval Times
n: Towns were generally unplanned, organically evolving with an irregular street pattern, and predominance of abbeys and cathedrals indicated church influence and control.

q: Under which presidential decree was the Mineral Reservations Development Board created?
ref: History of city planning: Marcos Regime
n: The Mineral Reservations Development Board was created under PD 1305.

q: Kenzo Tange's plan for Tokyo stressed which factor as a determinant of urban form?
ref: History of city planning: Kenzo Tange
n: Tange's plan for Tokyo emphasized circulation as a determinant of urban form.

q: The Human Settlements Regulatory Commission (HSRC), renamed from HSC in 1978 under Presidential Decree No. 1396, took on regulatory powers focusing on land use, zoning, and:
ref: History of city planning: Marcos Regime
n: HSRC focused on land use, zoning, and building regulations, approving subdivision and condominium plans and issuing development permits.

q: Frank Lloyd Wright's Broadacre City (1930s) symbolized his rejection of finance capital, landlordism and what else?
ref: History of city planning: Frank Lloyd Wright
n: Broadacre City symbolized rejection of finance capital and landlordism, an anarchist rejection of big government, while believing in the liberating effects of new technologies.

q: Which of these is NOT one of the functions of the Spanish colonial plaza?
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period — Functions of the Plaza
n: The plaza's functions listed are Social, Political, Economic, and Religious — an industrial function is not mentioned.

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: What did Robert Owen's New Lanark settlement (1800–1810) provide that was rare in industrial towns of the time?
o: Tall apartment towers set in open parkland
Communal living, central heating and family lodgings
Wide boulevards for carriages and trams
Detached houses each on an acre of land
ref: History of city planning: New Communities
n: New Lanark had 1,000-strong communities with residence near the workplace, communal living for old and young, central heating, and private lodging for families with children under 3.

q: Which body, formed after World War II, was the main national development planning agency and the forerunner of NEDA?
ref: History of city planning: Philippine Republic
n: The NPC was the main government body responsible for national development planning and precursor to NEDA.

q: The first garden city, established in 1902 about 35 miles from London and planned by Barry Parker and Raymond Unwin, was:
ref: History of city planning: Ebenezer Howard
n: In 1902, a garden city was established in Letchworth, 35 miles from London, planned by Barry Parker and Raymond Unwin.

q: Under the Aquino administration, the shift back to local governance and participation was formalized in which law?
o: Urban Development and Housing Act of 1992
ref: History of city planning: Aquino Regime
n: This period saw economic instability and discontinuity, with urban planning shifting back to local governance via the Local Government Code (LGC) of 1991.

q: Unlike the MMC, the MMDA has a "unique status" in that it coordinates with LGUs but does NOT have:
ref: History of city planning: Aquino/post-EDSA Era
n: MMDA's unique status is that it coordinates with LGUs but does not have legislative authority over them, and has limited enforcement powers compared to the MMC.

q: Under which presidential decree was the Human Settlements Commission (HSC) created in 1975?
ref: History of city planning: Marcos Regime
n: HSC was established in 1975 under Presidential Decree No. 933.

q: Benton Mackaye, originally a forester, viewed the nation's natural divisions as:
o: Climate zones drawn by rainfall alone
River drainage basins, not state lines
ref: History of city planning: Benton Mackaye
n: Mackaye saw the nation as a series of component parts whose natural divisions were river drainage areas, not state lines.

q: The basic socio-political unit during the Pre-Spanish Period, composed of 30–100 families ruled by kinship, was called:
ref: History of city planning: Pre-Spanish Period
n: The basic socio-political unit was the barangay, composed of 30–100 families ruled by kinship.

q: Which farm tool's spread gave rise to rectilinear land plotting in the ancient world?
ref: History of city planning: Ancient World
n: Rectilinear plotting used the plow, suited for land division for crop planning and land plotting after a flood along the Nile, Tigris, and Euphrates.

s: Ancient Greece (500–400 B.C.) — Hippodamus of Miletus
q: In ancient Greek town planning, which central open space was enclosed by buildings that served as its facades?
ref: History of city planning: Ancient Greece
n: The Agora's buildings served as facades forming an enclosed urban space, grouped around a central open space.

q: Lewis Mumford urged that the fundamental needs of society be the basis for the judicious use of:
ref: History of city planning: Lewis Mumford
n: Mumford urged that fundamental needs be the basis for judicious use of technological power, recognizing the physical limitations of human settlements.

q: In his "Codex Atlanticus", Leonardo da Vinci sketched a plan with a river split into 6 or 7 branches for which city?
ref: History of city planning: Rome 1500s
n: Da Vinci described a new urban planning concept suited for Milan, sketching a city straddling a river with its upstream divided into 6–7 branches rejoining below the city.

q: The New Communities' Movement's rallying cry was to produce not only better homes, but:
ref: History of city planning: New Communities' Movement
n: The movement's rallying cry was to produce better communities, not just better homes, with community problem issues discussed openly among planners.

q: Which capital city did Walter Burley Griffin (1876–1937) design?
ref: History of city planning: The City Beautiful Era
n: Walter Burley Griffin designed the Canberra plan.

q: In the Spanish colonial plaza complex, which building was usually the largest and most dominant?
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period — Key Elements
n: The Church was usually the largest and most dominant structure, often facing the setting sun and symbolizing the Church's central role.

q: During the American era, Daniel Burnham prepared plans for Manila and which new summer capital?
ref: History of city planning: American Era
n: Burnham's most significant projects were the remaking of Manila and the creation of an entirely new summer capital at Baguio.

q: By about what year had Rome become the first city with a population of one million?
ref: History of city planning: Ancient Rome
n: Rome was the first city with a million population, reached in 3 A.D.

q: Russian geographer Peter Kropotkin's "Fields, Factories, and Workshops" advocated combining agriculture and brainwork with:
ref: History of city planning
n: Kropotkin's book combined agriculture and brainwork with manual work, and suggested electricity could allow towns to be built anywhere, advocating minimal government and maximum self-sufficiency.

q: Under which body did the Ramos administration activate the Environmental Planning Board?
o: Housing and Land Use Regulatory Board
ref: History of city planning: Ramos Administration
n: The Ramos Administration activated the Environmental Planning Board under the PRC.

q: During the Commonwealth Period, planning institutions such as NUPC, CCPC, and RPB were created, bridging colonial planning with:
ref: History of city planning: Commonwealth Period
n: This period bridged colonial planning with Filipino leadership, laying the groundwork for local urban governance.

q: Which Roman architect wrote the ten-book "De Architectura", treating architecture and town design as one subject?
ref: History of city planning: Ancient Rome / Vitruvius
n: Vitruvius's 10-volume treatise "De Architectura" related Roman architecture and town design experience as a single theme.

q: Vitruvius's treatise laid the foundation of theoretical design thinking by addressing all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Location of streets relative to prevailing wind
ref: History of city planning: Ancient Rome / Vitruvius
n: Vitruvius addressed street orientation to wind, siting of public buildings, testing of drinking water, and design of plazas — steel-frame skyscrapers did not exist in his era.

q: Massive reconstruction efforts in the post-WWII Philippine Republic period were especially concentrated in:
ref: History of city planning: Philippine Republic
n: Massive reconstruction efforts were especially concentrated in Metro Manila.

q: Thomas Adams (1871–1940), one of the founding fathers of British Town Planning, served as the first general manager of:
ref: History of city planning: Thomas Adams
n: Adams was first general manager of Letchworth Garden City.

q: Buckminster Fuller's "Inventory of World Resources — Human Trends and Needs" (1963) assessed the world's production and productive energy and suggested it be turned to man's:
ref: History of city planning: Buckminster Fuller
n: Fuller assessed current world production/energy and suggested how it could be turned to man's complete advantage.

q: Charles Abrams saw housing as one of the prime fields for solving urban problems, writing:
o: The Human Use of Human Beings
Man's Struggle for Shelter in an Urbanizing World
ref: History of city planning: Charles Abrams
n: Abrams wrote "Man's Struggle for Shelter in an Urbanizing World" (1964), discussing housing's prime role in urban development and policy.

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: George Pullman, U.S. railroad engineer and inventor of Pullman cars, built his model industrial town outside Chicago (from 1880) on how many acres of wetland?
ref: History of city planning: New Communities
n: Pullman's model industrial town outside Chicago occupied 4,000 acres of wetland.

q: Ebenezer Howard showed how workable, livable towns could be formed within the capitalist framework through the:
ref: History of city planning: Ebenezer Howard
n: Howard's Social City concept involved decentralized employment, polycentric settlements, garden cities, and suburban expansion.

q: Antonio Kayanan, the "first Filipino planner", belongs to which era of national planning?
ref: History of city planning: Philippine Republic
n: Antonio Kayanan, the first Filipino planner, led national planning during the Philippine Republic period, including plans for Manila and Quezon City.

q: The Radburn idea created a series of "superblocks" — islands of green bordered by homes and skirted by peripheral auto roads — connected by pedestrian ways called:
ref: History of city planning: New Communities' Movement
n: The Radburn idea's pedestrian ways were called greenways, interconnecting open green spaces within each superblock.

q: Le Corbusier's Chandigarh was criticized as a visual, symbolic plan blind to the economic and human needs of which country's people?
ref: History of city planning: Le Corbusier
n: Critics noted his plan was completely impervious to the economic and human considerations of the Indian population.

q: Into which department was HLURB merged in 2019?
o: Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD)
Department of Public Works and Highways
Department of Interior and Local Government
ref: History of city planning: Aquino Regime
n: HLURB was merged into DHSUD in 2019.

s: The Regional Planning Association of America (RPAA)
q: The Regional Planning Association of America (RPAA), founded in 1923 from the close association of Mumford, Stein, MacKaye, and others, published a group manifesto called:
ref: History of city planning: RPAA
n: The RPAA published "Survey," one of the most important documents in planning history, devoted to the concept of the region.

q: Architect Lucio Costa's plan did not include a single population projection, economic analyses, land use schedule, model, or mechanical drawing, yet was awarded the commission for:
ref: History of city planning: Lucio Costa
n: Lucio Costa's scheme, despite lacking these typical elements, was awarded for Brasília, the new interior capital replacing an overburdened Rio de Janeiro.

q: The Housing and Land Use Regulatory Board (HLURB) worked with LGUs to guide the preparation of:
ref: History of city planning: Aquino Regime
n: HLURB worked with LGUs to guide comprehensive land use plans (CLUPs), part of its devolution of oversight functions.

q: The Garden City movement, dispersing people into self-contained towns in open country, was a response to which kind of city?
ref: History of city planning: Garden City Movement
n: The concept responded to the Victorian City by exploring the dispersal of people to new self-contained constellations of new towns built in open countryside.

q: John Nash's ambitious 1811 London concept connected the center of the city to a park at the city's edge via a grand avenue, resulting in the design of:
o: Hyde Park Corner and the Mall
ref: History of city planning
n: Nash's plan and carried-out work resulted in Regent Street, Regent Park, and Crescent.

q: In Alberti's "ideal cities," the star-shaped plan with radiating streets was usually proposed for a:
ref: History of city planning: Renaissance
n: The designs were usually proposed for a church, palace, or castle, with curved streets conforming to topography.

q: Le Corbusier unveiled his "Ville Contemporaine" in 1922 as a hypothetical plan for a city of how many people?
ref: History of city planning: Le Corbusier
n: The "Ville Contemporaine" was a hypothetical plan for a city of 3 million people, exploiting technology.

q: According to Daniel Burnham, the ideal city in the City Beautiful Era was a totally designed system of circulation arteries, parks, and civic center building blocks including all of the following EXCEPT:
ref: History of city planning: The City Beautiful Era
n: The civic center blocks listed are city hall, a country house, a library, an opera house, a museum, and a plaza — a factory district is not mentioned.

q: American architect-planner Clarence A. Perry's 1929 book, "The Neighborhood Unit," discussed organizing towns into cohesive neighborhoods based on the natural catchment area of community facilities such as:
ref: History of city planning: Clarence A. Perry
n: Perry's neighborhood principle was based on the natural catchment area of facilities such as a primary school and shops.

q: French planner Eugene Henard's "The Cities of the Future" envisioned buildings on stilts, traffic circles, and:
ref: History of city planning: Eugene Henard
n: Henard's vision included buildings on stilts, traffic circles, and airplane rooftop landings.

q: The Ramos Administration's economic development program focused on infrastructure such as power, telecom, LRT, MRT, flyovers, ports, and airports, alongside a mushrooming of:
ref: History of city planning: Ramos Administration
n: This period saw major infrastructure projects and the mushrooming of shopping malls throughout the country, plus the emergence of mixed-use development.

q: Lewis Mumford's influential 1961 book on the history and prospects of the city is titled:
ref: History of city planning: Lewis Mumford
n: Mumford wrote "The City in History" (1961).

q: Known as a "Master Builder," Robert Moses was in charge of the implementation of:
ref: History of city planning: Robert Moses
n: Robert Moses, Master Builder, was in charge of implementing the New York Plan.

q: Under which law was the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) created in 1995?
ref: History of city planning: Aquino/post-EDSA Era
n: MMDA was created in 1995 under Republic Act No. 7924.

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: William Lever's model village for his soap factory employees on the Mersey (1888), featuring cottages with small back gardens, was called:
ref: History of city planning: New Communities
n: William Lever relocated his chemical/soap factory to Port Sunlight, more of a village for his employees with cottages and small back gardens.

q: The Spanish colonial "Plaza Complex" planning model used in the Philippines was based on the Spanish royal decree known as the:
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period
n: The Plaza Complex was based on the "Laws of the Indies," a royal decree prescribing how colonial towns should be planned.

q: The Municipal Hall (Casa Real/Ayuntamiento) in a Spanish-era plaza complex was the seat of local colonial government, representing:
ref: History of city planning: Spanish Period — Key Elements
n: The Municipal Hall was the seat of local colonial government, representing civil authority.

s: New Communities Built Around New Factories
q: What is the name of the model mill town Titus Salt built near Bradford, England (1853–1863)?
ref: History of city planning: New Communities
n: Titus Salt built Saltaire, a model industrial community with a monotonous but easily accessible layout near open country.

q: Louis Kahn's important designs for Central Philadelphia organized circulation — main arterial stop-and-go streets and parking towers — into what he called a:
ref: History of city planning: Louis Kahn
n: Kahn organized urban form into a "symphony of circulation."

q: Baron Georges-Eugène Haussmann was tasked by Napoleon III in 1853 to rebuild Paris, a project regarded as:
o: The first garden city in continental Europe
The first zoning ordinance in any city
History's largest public works project to date
The first regional plan for a capital
ref: History of city planning: Paris 1800s
n: The rebuilding of Paris entailed tearing down many houses and was history's largest public works project.

q: HSRC was renamed HLURB in 1986 after which event?
ref: History of city planning: Aquino Regime
n: HSRC was renamed HLURB in 1986 after the EDSA Revolution.

q: Which city did Biagio Rossetti extend with the Addizione Erculea (1492), making it 'the first modern city in Europe'?
ref: History of city planning: Renaissance era entries
n: Biagio Rossetti's Addizione Erculea (1492) doubled Ferrara with a regular grid; Burckhardt called it the first modern city in Europe.

q: Don Arturo Soria y Mata's 1882 proposal for a "Linear City" set houses and buildings along what?
o: A ring railway around the old city walls
A central plaza with radiating avenues
A river canal lined with warehouses
Linear utilities: water, power and a rail line
ref: History of city planning
n: Soria y Mata proposed that the logic of linear utility lines should be the basis of all city layout, with houses set alongside them.

q: During the pre-Spanish period, informal Philippine settlement planning was influenced mainly by which settlers?
ref: History of city planning: Pre-Spanish Period
n: Planning during this time was informal and community-based, largely influenced by Chinese and Malay settlers.

q: French social reformer Charles Fourier's 1829 publication, "The New World of Industry and Society," envisioned putting 400 families into a palace-like building called:
ref: History of city planning
n: Fourier envisioned putting 400 families into a palace-like building he called the "Phalanstery."

q: The National Economic Council (NEC), which handled economic policy and national investment programs, was eventually merged into:
ref: History of city planning: Philippine Republic
n: NEC was merged into NEDA, playing a crucial role in infrastructure and regional development planning before that.

q: Sir Christopher Wren prepared a plan for London proposing a network of avenues connecting the main features of London, including:
o: The Tower of London and London Bridge
St. Peter's and St. Paul Cathedral
ref: History of city planning: London 1600s
n: Wren prepared a plan for London including St. Peter's and St. Paul Cathedral, proposing a network of avenues connecting London's main features.

s: Town & Country Planning Act of 1947 in Britain
q: A radical change in new-town concept introduced in the 1950s plan for "Hook" involved houses grouped very closely along a:
ref: History of city planning: Town & Country Planning Act
n: In the Hook plan, houses were closely grouped along a multi-level linear spine, decreasing distances to communal facilities.

q: Jane Jacobs' (1962) book, one of the most influential in the history of city planning, is titled:
o: "The Death and Life of Great American Cities"
ref: History of city planning: Jane Jacobs
n: Jane Jacobs wrote "The Death and Life of Great American Cities."

q: Norbert Wiener, who wrote "The Human Use of Human Beings" (1950), proposed a study of automatic control systems known as:
ref: History of city planning: Norbert Wiener
n: Wiener proposed cybernetics — the science of controls and communication in the animal and the machine.
